check: does any test still assume the old corridorHalfWidth of 192, which would invalidate the pending GameTest run
why: The goal says the old baseline is invalid because corridorHalfWidth moved from 192 to 512. If a test still hardcoded 192 the pending run would be measuring against a stale assumption rather than the current configuration.
sweepResult: Seven occurrences of the literal 192 exist across src/test and src/gametest. None is the corridor value.
eachOccurrence: AdjacentComponentMatrixTests line 402 - gap(96, 192), an island gap coordinate
ColdCaptureAllocationTests line 72 - a 192-byte point allowance, a byte count in an assertion message
CurvedWallMatrixTests line 53 - a sampling loop from -192 to 192 in x
RampGroundPortalTests lines 21 and 22 - an index comparison and an attempted count, both iteration counts
ReservationHeapPressureTest line 79 - compiledComponents 192, a component count in reported JSON
GroundExitResolverTest line 66 - 192*256L, an SQ8 arc coordinate

positiveConfirmation.fixturesUse512: Four fixtures construct GenerationConfig with the seventh argument as 512: AdjacentComponentMatrixTests line 750, PipelineReservationHandoffAuditTests line 132, ProductionPipelineTests line 133 and SiteRuntimeIndexGameTests line 58
positiveConfirmation.fieldOrderVerified: WallTypes declares GenerationConfig as algorithmVersion, templateVersion, segmentBlocks, stationBlocks, columnBudget, carrierAmplitude, corridorHalfWidth, maxGeometryInflight, segmentBytes, terrainBytes, compiledBytes - so the seventh argument is indeed corridorHalfWidth
positiveConfirmation.runtimeGuard: RidgePlanner line 30 throws unless columnBudget is 150000 and corridorHalfWidth is 512, so anything reaching the planner must already carry 512

anApparentContradictionPursuedAndDismiss.observation: Those same fixtures pass 256 as carrierAmplitude, while AnchorField line 19 throws unless segmentBlocks is 2048 and carrierAmplitude is 384.
anApparentContradictionPursuedAndDismiss.whyItIsNotADefect: None of the four constructs AnchorField or RidgePlanner - each has zero such constructions - so the frozen 384 guard is never reached. They exercise the pipeline, reservation and allocation layers using a synthetic config where that field is not load-bearing.
anApparentContradictionPursuedAndDismiss.methodNote: This looked like a genuine contradiction, and the check that settled it was counting constructor calls in the tests rather than reasoning about the numbers.

conclusion: No stale 192 assumption remains. The fixtures carry 512, and the planner enforces it at runtime, so the pending run will measure the current configuration.
